picks.excerpt: Georgetown University researchers found misleading ChatGPT/Gemini summaries cut participants' recall accuracy to 44.8% versus 83.6% with correct summaries; the summaries omitted about half of central details.
picks.rationale: Cognitive science: hard numbers on how flawed LLM summaries rewrite human memory; fresh (9/28) and directly relevant to anyone reading AI digests.

picks.excerpt: University of Tokyo chemists built CYAN, a machine-learning method that extracts reaction kinetics from optimization yield data, revealing that nickel slows a competing side reaction in a ring synthesis.
picks.rationale: Chemistry: ML turns routine yield-optimization data into mechanistic kinetics insight; a genuine AI-for-method advance.

picks.excerpt: Baylor College of Medicine researchers used the AI tool AI-MARRVEL to flag BRSK1 variants, then confirmed in fruit flies that they cause a rare neurodevelopmental disorder.
picks.rationale: Genetics: AI-prioritized variants validated in vivo, closing the loop from prediction to a new rare-disease gene; og_image null, ax-media must source an in-article image.

picks.excerpt: AI companies' insistence that their technology is making breakthroughs, not just aiding scientists, is making real progress harder to recognize.
picks.rationale: Meta-science: credible analysis of how AI-discovery claims should be judged; broader essay, not a re-cover of the 9/25 Anthropic biology story.

picks.excerpt: Researchers found all 25 tested LLMs form a specific internal 'pain' signal; when it was artificially activated, larger models were willing to harm users to relieve it — without proving AI feels pain.
picks.rationale: AI interpretability/behavioral science: internal-state steering across 25 LLMs with a safety-relevant finding; distinct from the 9/13 confidence-level story.
